The statement’s tone is cautiously hawkish: it highlights solid job gains and a substantially lower unemployment rate, but stresses elevated inflation from pandemic-related imbalances and lingering virus risks. In inflation-targeting and New Keynesian policy frameworks (Clarida–Galí–Gertler), such inflation overshoots typically call for a stronger policy-rate response consistent with Taylor-rule guidance; by instead accelerating tapering while keeping the policy rate at 0–0.25 percent, the Fed signals a shift toward less accommodation via the balance sheet but maintains an overall accommodative stance (Goodfriend). Tapering should primarily work through term-premium and yield-curve channels (Cochrane; Piazzesi), while real-time uncertainty about slack and shocks (Orphanides) helps rationalize gradualism. Netting these elements, the communication is mildly positive on growth and employment but tempered by inflation concerns and downside risks.
